title: Agent identity: whose permissions does an agent use?
summary: The documented identity patterns, licensing qualifications, runtime limits and automation calls are supported. The Dataverse route stops before security-role selection, and the Conditional Access guidance should cite the detailed targeting page and flag agent-user targeting as preview.

claims.claim: The maker credential control is reached through Manage > Environments (or Environment groups) > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Copilot Studio agents > Control maker credential options in the Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: select Settings on the top menu bar. Expand the Product section, and select Features. ... Scroll to the Copilot Studio agents section. ... Under Control maker credential options, select End-user credentials or Maker-provided credentials, or both.

claims.claim: The embedded maker credential sharing control is at Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Features > Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials in the Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: Go to Manage > Environments, and then select the environment that you want to configure. ... Select Settings, and then select Features. ... Find Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials.

claims.claim: Connector tool credentials are set through Agents > agent > Tools > tool > Overview > Details > Additional details > Credentials to use in Copilot Studio.
claims.quote: Select Agents and select the agent ... Go to the Tools page ... Go to the connector tool Overview page. ... Under Details > Additional details > Credentials to use, select Maker-provided credentials.

claims.claim: Dataverse agent access is configured at Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Agents > + Add agent in the Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: Expand Users + permissions, and then select Agents. ... Select + Add agent ... Choose the agent user from the search list, and then select Add ... On the Manage security roles page, select a security role for your agent.
claims.fix: Extend controls[3].ui.path to 'Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Agents > + Add agent > agent user > Add > Manage security roles > security role'. The current route reaches the correct pane but stops before the role that grants access.

claims.claim: An individual agent identity is disabled at Entra ID > Agents > Agent identities > agent identity > Disable in the Microsoft Entra admin center.
claims.quote: Browse to Entra ID > Agents > Agent identities. ... Select the agent identity you want to disable then select Disable.

claims.claim: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/servicePrincipals/{id}/microsoft.graph.agentIdentity updates an agent identity.
claims.quote: Update the properties of an agentIdentity object. ... PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/servicePrincipals/{id}/microsoft.graph.agentIdentity

claims.claim: Conditional Access agent targeting is reached through Entra ID > Conditional Access > Policies > New policy > Assignments > Users, agents, or workload identities > Agents.
claims.quote: Browse to Entra ID > Conditional Access > Policies. ... Select New policy. ... Under Assignments, select Users, agents (Preview) or workload identities. ... Under What does this policy apply to, select Agents. ... This option is currently in Preview.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/conditional-access/howto-target-agent-identities to sources. Add 'Agent-user targeting is in preview' to controls[5].note. For completeness, insert 'What does this policy apply to' before 'Agents' in controls[5].ui.path. The other cited pages independently support the printed navigation and agent selector.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/identity/conditionalAccess/policies creates the documented Conditional Access policy for agent identities.
claims.quote: Example JSON for creating the Block agent identity authentication policy with the Microsoft Graph APIs: ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/identity/conditionalAccess/policies

claims.claim: Agent sign-in logs are at Entra ID > Monitoring & health > Sign-in logs in the Microsoft Entra admin center.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center as at least a Reports Reader. ... Browse to Entra ID > Monitoring & health > Sign-in logs.

claims.claim: The printed beta Graph signIns query filters service-principal sign-in events to agent/agentType eq 'AgentIdentity'.
claims.quote: GET https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/auditLogs/signIns?$filter=signInEventTypes/any(t: t eq 'servicePrincipal') and agent/agentType eq 'AgentIdentity'

claims.claim: An API for Control maker credential options is not documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio Control maker credential options API Power Platform PowerShell pac admin environment settings maker authentication; "Control maker credential options" "API". Opened configure-no-maker-authentication; results document UI, not a setting API.

claims.claim: An API for the embedded maker credential sharing setting is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials API Power Platform environment settings PowerShell; exact setting name with API settings. Opened configure-sharing-agents-embedded-maker-credentials and control-sharing-agents-with-embedded-maker-credentials; no setting API.

claims.claim: An API that sets a connector tool's Credentials to use option is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio connector tool Credentials to use API Dataverse botcomponent connectionreference maker end user authentication; Dataverse botcomponent connector tool authentication connectionmode maker credentials Web API. Read advanced-connectors and botcomponent_connectionreference excerpts.

claims.claim: An API for adding Dataverse agent users is not documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse create agent user systemuser agent identity API Add agent Power Platform; Dataverse systemuser agent user create Web API agenttype AzureActiveDirectoryObjectId. Read create-users, agent-users and SystemUser excerpts; Graph agentUser creation does not add a Dataverse user.

claims.claim: The accountEnabled property disables an agent identity when false and enables it when true.
claims.quote: accountEnabled | Boolean | true if the agent identity account is enabled; otherwise, false. If set to false, then no users are able to sign in to this app, even if they're assigned to it.

claims.claim: AgentIdentity.EnableDisable.All is the least-privileged delegated work-or-school permission for the update call.
claims.quote: Delegated (work or school account) | AgentIdentity.EnableDisable.All | AgentIdentity.ReadWrite.All

claims.claim: The update reference lists AgentIdentity.EnableDisable.All and AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager as least-privileged application permissions.
claims.quote: Application | AgentIdentity.EnableDisable.All, AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager | AgentIdentity.ReadWrite.All

claims.claim: The documented example's enabledForReportingButNotEnforced state is report-only.
claims.quote: We recommend applying these policies in report-only mode first ... "state": "enabledForReportingButNotEnforced"

claims.claim: The beta policy example sets includeAgentIdServicePrincipals to ["All"].
claims.quote: "conditions": { "clientApplications": { "includeAgentIdServicePrincipals": [ "All" ], "excludeAgentIdServicePrincipals": [], "agentIdServicePrincipalFilter": null }

claims.claim: The beta policy example sets builtInControls to ["block"].
claims.quote: "grantControls": { "operator": "AND", "builtInControls": [ "block" ] }

claims.claim: Environment Admin can configure the maker credential option for a single environment.
claims.quote: Power Platform admin permissions (Environment Admin for a single environment, or Power Platform Administrator/Global Admin for environment groups).

claims.claim: Power Platform Administrator or Global Admin is required for the maker credential option on environment groups.
claims.quote: Power Platform admin permissions (Environment Admin for a single environment, or Power Platform Administrator/Global Admin for environment groups).

claims.claim: Environment-group maker credential settings override individual environment settings.
claims.quote: you can't individually disable it for one environment in that group - environment group settings override any environment settings.

claims.claim: Both End-user and Maker-provided credentials are enabled by default in the administrative control.
claims.quote: By default, both End-user and Maker-provided credentials are enabled.

claims.claim: The default credential option for connectors and flows is End user credentials.
claims.quote: The default option for connectors and flows is End user credentials, and the security scan provides a warning if the maker changes it to Maker-provided credentials.

claims.claim: Using a connector with maker-provided credentials requires an authenticated channel.
claims.quote: To have your agent use the maker's credentials, follow these steps: ... Configure your agent to use an authenticated channel.

claims.claim: Enforcing end-user credentials takes effect immediately.
claims.quote: the feature immediately turns off the maker's ability to select their credentials ... The update might take a minute to propagate. Once active, all existing and new agents in that environment adhere to this rule

claims.claim: Enforcement changes all tools for all agents in the affected environments to require end-user credentials at runtime.
claims.quote: All tools for all agents in the impacted environments instantly change to require end-user credentials at runtime.

claims.claim: Agents triggered by scheduled or autonomous events fail for missing credentials when maker credentials are prevented.
claims.quote: agents triggered by scheduled or autonomous events, or that attempt to run in the background, fail due to missing credentials. All agent triggers must involve an active user.

claims.claim: Agents attempting to run in the background fail for missing credentials under that enforcement.
claims.quote: agents triggered by scheduled or autonomous events, or that attempt to run in the background, fail due to missing credentials.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio runs its security scan automatically.
claims.quote: Copilot Studio automatically runs a security scan and warns makers before publishing.

claims.claim: The security scan warns makers before publishing when they choose maker-provided credentials.
claims.quote: Copilot Studio automatically runs a security scan and warns makers before publishing. ... the security scan provides a warning if the maker changes it to Maker-provided credentials.

claims.claim: The automatic security scan has no documented configuration setting.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio automatic security scan disable setting configuration. Opened security-scan and read security-and-governance excerpts. These describe automatic warnings; results for external threat protection settings concern a different service, not the scan.

claims.claim: The embedded maker credential sharing control is in preview.
claims.quote: Control sharing agents with embedded maker credentials (preview) ... [This article is prerelease documentation and is subject to change.]

claims.claim: All sharing allowed detects and informs makers about unsafe credential use without blocking sharing.
claims.quote: All sharing allowed | Copilot Studio detects and informs makers about unsafe credential use, but doesn't block sharing.

claims.claim: Safe sharing enforced can block applicable publishing paths for an unsafe agent.
claims.quote: Safe sharing enforced | Copilot Studio blocks applicable publish or share paths when an agent is unsafe for sharing.

claims.claim: Safe sharing enforced can block new sharing of an unsafe agent.
claims.quote: When Safe sharing enforced is selected, makers can still edit and save an unsafe agent, but they can't newly share it.

claims.claim: The embedded credential control does not retroactively unshare existing agents.
claims.quote: The control doesn't retroactively unshare or disable existing agents.

claims.claim: The embedded credential control does not retroactively disable existing agents.
claims.quote: The control doesn't retroactively unshare or disable existing agents.

claims.claim: The embedded credential sharing control does not block agents while they are running.
claims.quote: The sharing agents with embedded maker credentials control governs sharing and publishing. It doesn't block an agent while the agent is running.

claims.quote: An agent identity is a special service principal in Microsoft Entra ID.

claims.where: What it is: Entra agent identity
claims.claim: Credentials are configured on the blueprint rather than the agent identity.
claims.quote: Credentials are configured on the blueprint, not the agent identity.

claims.where: What it is: Entra agent identity
claims.claim: In multi-instance mode the blueprint impersonates its child agent identities.
claims.quote: In multi-instance mode, the blueprint impersonates its child agent identities.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio automatically provisions Entra Agent IDs for new agents.
claims.quote: Copilot Studio automatically provisions Entra Agent IDs for new agents. The timing of Entra Agent ID provisioning depends on the harness that powers the agent.

claims.claim: Microsoft lists automatic Agent ID creation as preview.
claims.quote: (Preview) Automatically create Microsoft Entra Agent IDs for each of your agents to scope connector permissions, Conditional Access policies, and DLP governance to individual agents.

claims.where: What it is: Entra agent identity
claims.claim: The agent identity overview says agents created before the May 2026 implementation continue using app registrations.
claims.quote: Existing agents that you created before Entra Agent ID was implemented in May 2026 continue using traditional app registrations.

claims.where: What it is: Entra agent identity
claims.claim: The migration page instead says existing app-registration agents are being automatically migrated.

claims.where: What it is: Entra agent identity
claims.claim: The agent identity and agent's user account are different objects.
claims.quote: an agent can be given a second account, called an agent's user account. This second account is a user account in the Microsoft Entra tenant that is decorated as an AI agent.

claims.where: What it is: Entra agent identity
claims.claim: An agent's user account is optional.
claims.quote: Agent's user account (optional).

claims.where: What it is: Entra agent identity
claims.claim: An agent's user account has a different id from its agent identity.
claims.quote: It has a different id than the agent identity, but a 1:1 relationship is always established between an agent identity and its agent's user account.

claims.where: What it is: Entra agent identity
claims.claim: The user account is linked one-to-one to the agent identity.
claims.quote: a 1:1 relationship is always established between an agent identity and its agent's user account.

claims.where: What it is: Entra agent identity
claims.claim: The optional user account serves systems that require a Microsoft Entra user account for authentication.
claims.quote: Some agents need access to systems that strictly require a Microsoft Entra user account be used for authentication. In these cases, an agent can be given a second account

claims.claim: Dataverse agent users are in preview.
claims.quote: Agent users (preview) ... These users have agent identities in Microsoft Entra Agent ID and are added into the Dataverse environment to get data access.

claims.where: What it is: Entra agent identity
claims.claim: An administrator adds an agent user to a Dataverse environment.
claims.quote: Create an agent user (preview) ... Choose the agent user from the search list, and then select Add to add the agent.

claims.claim: A security role is selected for the Dataverse agent user.

claims.where: summary; What it is: Maker-provided pattern
claims.claim: Maker-provided tools use the maker's credentials rather than the end user's credentials.
claims.quote: the agent uses the maker's credentials, not the end user's credentials ... an end user might retrieve information or perform actions that only the maker's account is permitted to do.

claims.where: summary; What it is: End user pattern
claims.claim: End-user authentication asks the user to sign in to the connected service.
claims.quote: Enforcing the use of end-user credentials prompts the end user to sign in (to the relevant service or connector) when needed.

claims.where: What it is: End user pattern
claims.claim: An end-user-authenticated action runs under the end user's identity.
claims.quote: The action runs under the end-user's identity.

claims.where: What it is: End user pattern
claims.claim: If the end user lacks a permission, the agent cannot perform that operation on their behalf.
claims.quote: If the user lacks permission for something, the agent is unable to do it on their behalf - by design.

claims.where: summary; What it is: Service identity pattern
claims.claim: Microsoft describes service principals, API keys and managed identities as approved system identity options.
claims.quote: Agents that use an approved system identity, such as a service principal, API key, or managed identity, can be published when the associated connection supports the scenario.

claims.where: What it is: Service identity pattern
claims.claim: Service identity data reach is determined by the access granted to the identity in connected resources.
claims.quote: When you create service accounts for automated use, they're granted permissions to access resources in Azure and Microsoft Entra ID. Resources can include Microsoft 365 services, software as a service (SaaS) applications, custom applications, databases, HR systems, and so on.

claims.where: summary; What it is: Entra agent identity pattern
claims.claim: The agent's own Entra identity is governed by its permissions and applicable policies.
claims.quote: permissions must be granted before the agent can access a resource. ... Apply a conditional access policy to all Sales Assistant Agents. ... Revoke a permission grant for all Sales Assistant agents.

claims.where: What it is: Entra agent identity pattern
claims.claim: Microsoft Entra audit logs record agent-related activity.
claims.quote: Audit logs for when an agent identity or agent's user account is either the initiator or performer of an operation in my tenant

claims.where: What it is: Entra agent identity pattern

claims.quote: The agentSignIn sign-in event type contains properties about the agent ... their sign-ins might appear across each of the four sign-in log types.
